A language is a dialect with an army. As far as I know, the differences are only in spoken language, not in written language, so it probably wouldn't qualify.

And even mainland Spanish itself isn't really an unified language to the degree that American or British English are, but the Castilian dialect imposed on everyone else in official communication, with differences going from mild (Aragonese) to crossing over into an entirely new language (Catalan).

I don't actually think they are different languages but the variations are interesting enough to explore.

The differences are greater spoken than written. There are significant differences in vocabulary. Mexican Spanish borrows a lot from Indian languages. Both are Castilian in origin. The Mexican version predictably more archaic.

A switchblade is a self-opening lockblade knife. Lockblades are much safer to use the jackknives, and a self-opening knife requires only one hand, which can be life-saving in some emergency situations.

Assisted-opening knives, which require one hand and the flick of a finger, are fully legal, but switchblades, which require one hand and the press of a button, are not legal. It makes no sense.
